narrative.overview: Morning Paper should feel like a serious personal machine for reading: tactile, intelligent, independent. The system sits between algorithmic and analog. It uses agents and source files to build a reader-owned algorithm, then lands the result as a finite edition that can be read, marked up, and improved tomorrow.
keyCharacteristics: Print-first, with the PDF as the proof.
Source-aware, finite, and skeptical of single-source truth.
Visual metaphors backed by durable newsroom files.
Calm enough to read, distinct enough to remember.

rules.name: The Ink First Rule
rules.body: Start with ink, rule, weight, and position. Add color only when it clarifies status, source, or proof.

rules.name: The No Feed Chrome Rule
rules.body: Never import social-platform color systems into the paper. X, RSS, GitHub, and inbox material become Morning Paper material.

rules.name: The No Costume Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears when the content is literally a command, code block, or log. It is not the brand voice.

rules.name: The Flat Proof Rule
rules.body: A proof surface earns trust through hierarchy, source notes, and status, not floating cards.

dos: Do make the rendered paper or proof artifact the center of every brand and product surface.
Do use newsroom language when it clarifies a real role, file, source state, or proof step.
Do keep color sparse, semantic, and monochrome-safe.
Do show source diversity, missing perspectives, prior mentions, and extraction limits when trust is the point.
donts: Don't make this a generic AI dashboard.
Don't default to Vercel-style developer polish or Factory AI-style agent machinery.
Don't create cutesy agent roleplay unless the user explicitly asks for an optional experimental surface.
Don't build another beige productivity app.
